title: Extraordinary mechanical properties of AZ61 alloy processed by ECAP with 160 degree channel angle and EPT

nodes.label: Wrought Mg alloys trade strength against ductility; AZ61 needs both without rare-earth additions
Storing dislocations by low-strain ECAP and then recrystallising them statically with a short electropulse should give ultrafine equiaxed grains with strength and ductility together
Commercial hot-extruded AZ61 (Mg-6Al-1Zn) plate, billets 10 x 10 x 70 mm
ECAP through a shallow die, intersection angle 160 deg and outer curvature 20 deg, route Bc at 4 mm/s

attrs.purpose: low strain per pass so dislocations accumulate without recrystallising

nodes.label: ECAP at 373, 423 and 473 K for 2-8 passes; electropulsing at 25-50 us pulse duration for 5-20 min

attrs.variables: ECAP temperature and passes, EPT pulse duration and time

nodes.label: Homogenise the billets at 623 K for 4 h before pressing
Screening ECAP: 2-5 passes at each of 373, 423 and 473 K
Single-temperature ECAP gives either an underdeformed billet that fractures by the fifth pass at 373 K or a dynamically recrystallised structure at 423-473 K
The ECAP temperature sets a balance: too low and the billet cannot take the strain, too high and dynamic recrystallisation consumes the stored energy
Adopt variable-temperature ECAP: 8 passes at 423 K followed by 3 passes at 373 K

attrs.basis_of_choice: accumulate strain warm, then add strain cold without triggering recrystallisation

nodes.label: Variable-temperature ECAP: 8 passes at 423 K then 3 passes at 373 K
After variable-temperature ECAP the grains are refined but elongated and not equiaxed, so dynamic recrystallisation is incomplete
The incomplete recrystallisation leaves a high stored dislocation density
Electropulsing treatment at 25 us pulse duration for 10 min
The pulse completes static recrystallisation at an average grain size near 1 um, from 89 um in the starting plate
The recrystallised structure has a weak basal texture, maximum 3.85 mrd, and a boundary population dominated by high-angle boundaries
Yield strength 330 MPa and tensile strength 448 MPa, against 100 and 260 MPa as received
Elongation to failure reaches 15%, against 7% for the 4-pass 373 K ECAP state
The pulse erases the dislocation strengthening, but the further grain refinement and texture weakening more than repay it, so strength and ductility rise together

attrs.mechanism_class: recovery and static recrystallisation against grain-boundary strengthening

nodes.label: Variable-temperature 160 deg ECAP followed by a short electropulse gives AZ61 an ultrafine grain size with 330 MPa YS, 448 MPa UTS and 15% elongation
The yield stress is the sum of grain-boundary, precipitation and dislocation strengthening contributions
The strength-ductility combination sits above every literature AZ61 processed by conventional deformation or other severe plastic deformation routes
The sub-2 um grain claims rest on optical micrographs that cannot resolve grains of that size; only the SEM and EBSD panels do
The panel credited with uniform ultrafine equiaxed grains shows a fine but clearly elongated lath structure, closer to the deformed panel of the same figure
The texture is called weakened although no as-received or as-ECAPed pole figure is shown as a baseline
The starting plate has abnormally coarse grains averaging 89 um, with a necklace of fine grains that homogenisation absorbs
Fine bright second-phase particles, taken as Mg17Al12, decorate the boundaries and grain interiors after electropulsing
Electropulsing removes the tangled dislocations, so the dislocation-strengthening share of the yield stress falls relative to the as-ECAPed state
As-extruded grains are tens of micrometres across with a necklace of much finer grains on their boundaries; after homogenisation the necklace is gone and the grains are coarser and heavily twinned

attrs.image_note: sized against the 50 um bars in both panels; the largest grains fill much of the field, consistent with but not resolving the quoted 89 um average

nodes.label: At 423 K slip and twin bands thicken from 2 to 4 passes and by 5 passes dark fine-grained recrystallised patches occupy much of the field

attrs.image_note: all four panels carry 50 um bars; at 5 passes the recrystallised patches cover roughly half the field, not 'most of the areas' as the text says, and the 373 K and 473 K series were not opened

nodes.label: After 8 passes at 423 K the etched structure is fine and directional, and after 3 further passes at 373 K it is finer still and remains directional

panel_conditions.condition: after 8-pass at 423 K / then 3-pass ECAP at 373 K

attrs.image_note: both panels carry 10 um bars (OCR cue); at that optical magnification the individual grains are not resolved and only the overall etch texture can be judged

nodes.label: Across the pulse series the structure goes from deformed laths at 30 us-5 min to equiaxed grains of about 2 um at 7 min and 3 um at 10 min, while 25 us-10 min gives features of about 0.5-1 um

panel_conditions.condition: 30 us-5 min / 30 us-7 min / 30 us-10 min / 25 us-10 min sample

attrs.image_note: all four SEM panels carry 2 um bars (OCR cue); sizes measured against them

nodes.label: The 25 us-10 min panel shows fine elongated lath-like features aligned in one direction, much like the deformed 30 us-5 min panel and unlike the equiaxed panels between them

attrs.image_note: audit node: the figure shows the discrepancy with the text, which reads this panel as uniform ultrafine equiaxed grains of about 1 um

nodes.label: Bright sub-micron particles are scattered over boundaries and grain interiors in every panel of the pulse series

attrs.image_note: the particles are well under the 2 um bar and no composition measurement accompanies them, so the Mg17Al12 identification is not made in this figure

nodes.label: The orientation maps give densely packed equiaxed grains of about 1-2 um for the 25 us sample and about 3-5 um for the 30 us sample

panel_conditions.condition: 25 us-10 min sample / 30 us-10 min sample

attrs.image_note: sized against the 5 um bars on the two maps; colours are random-orientation IPF colours, so grain identity is read from colour boundaries

nodes.label: The (0001) pole figures give maxima of 3.85 mrd for the 25 us sample and 4.57 mrd for the 30 us sample, with the density concentrated off-centre toward TD

attrs.image_note: maxima are printed under each pole figure; the OCR cue line mistakes the 4.57 mrd maximum for a 4.57 um scale bar. No as-received or as-ECAPed pole figure is shown, so there is no baseline for a weakening claim

nodes.label: Both misorientation histograms carry a tall spike below about 3 deg plus a broad band peaking near 30 deg, which spreads out toward 90 deg for the longer pulse

attrs.image_note: judge retype: a misorientation-angle histogram is the spread of a non-imaged quantity over the boundary ensemble, not a metric of imaged features, so this is OBS/response/distribution read by read_distribution_statistics. The sub-3 deg spike is the tallest bin in both panels (0.155 and 0.068 frequency), which the quoted 20% low-angle fraction does not obviously reflect; the panel prints no cumulative fractions

nodes.label: The variable-temperature plus 25 us-10 min curve yields near 330 MPa, peaks at about 448 MPa and fails at true strain 0.148, above the two other pulsed states

attrs.image_note: read against the panel's stress and true-strain axes; the other two curves peak at about 370 MPa (strain 0.17) and 357 MPa (strain 0.195) from lower yield points

nodes.label: On the UTS versus YS plane the three points of this work sit above and to the right of every literature point for AZ61

attrs.image_note: the best point reads about 335 MPa YS and 448 MPa UTS; the literature cluster spans 70-240 MPa YS and 175-320 MPa UTS

nodes.label: Baseline tensile values: as received 100 MPa YS, 260 MPa UTS and 16% elongation; 4-pass 373 K ECAP 300 MPa, 360 MPa and 7%
A 160 deg ECAP die imposes only about 0.2 equivalent strain per pass, far less than a 90 deg die
Hall-Petch: the strength of a bulk metal rises as the grain size falls
Mg17Al12 precipitates form in AZ61 during deformation and thermal cycling and pin dislocations
A weak basal texture and a high high-angle boundary fraction let non-basal slip and boundary sliding operate, raising ductility in Mg
Electropulsing delivers a high peak current density whose electron-wind force drives dislocation motion and recrystallisation nucleation

notes: Screen-then-choose process paper: the single-temperature ECAP trials (n7a -> n11) feed the mechanism n10 that motivates the variable-temperature down-select n9, and the spine then runs ECAP -> stored dislocations -> electropulse -> ultrafine grains and weak texture -> strength and ductility, closed by the trade-off n18 with its counteracts edge from the lost dislocation strengthening n27. Numbers are read from the panels: 330/448 MPa and true strain 0.148 from F13, 335/448 MPa against the literature cluster from F14, grain sizes against the 2 um bars of F10 and the 5 um bars of F11, pole-figure maxima 3.85 and 4.57 mrd printed on F11. Three audits. n22 with OBS o3: the sub-2 um grain claims of Figures 6 and 10 are made from optical micrographs at 10 um bars that cannot resolve them. n23 with OBS o5: the 25 us-10 min panel credited with uniform ultrafine equiaxed grains shows a fine but clearly elongated, directional lath structure, closer to the deformed 30 us-5 min panel than to the equiaxed 7 and 10 min panels. n24 with OBS o8: no as-received or as-ECAPed pole figure is shown, so 'weakened basal texture' has no baseline in the figure, and the only in-figure comparison gives the longer pulse the stronger maximum. Also noted: at 5 passes and 423 K the recrystallised patches cover about half the field rather than 'most areas'; the sub-3 deg spike is the tallest bin of both misorientation histograms, which the quoted 20% LAGB fraction does not obviously reflect; and the captions of Figures 8 and 9 give pass counts (4-pass at 423 K, 3-pass at 473 K) that the linked text reverses. OCR defects: the F11c cue line reads the texture maximum 'Max=4.57' as a 4.57 um scale bar, and the F11b/F11d cue lines type the misorientation histograms as XRD. Figure 1 is tier C with no panels offered. Lost: the 373 K and 473 K micrograph series (F3, F5), the EPT series on the single-temperature samples (F7-F9), the stress-strain curves of the as-ECAPed states (F12), the YS-versus-pass plot (F15) and Tables 1-4.

changes: o9: type changed from OBS/morphology/feature_metric to OBS/response/distribution, and the mm_op on o9 -> n15 from measure_feature_metric to read_distribution_statistics. F11b and F11d are misorientation-angle histograms, i.e. the spread of a non-imaged quantity over the boundary ensemble read from a plotted distribution, not a metric measured on imaged features. The v04 rule 'read from a plotted quantity -> response' applies. Panel ids, modality (bar chart -> xy_curve), image_support and the reading itself are unchanged.

panel_checks.note: Both crops opened at their 2 um bars. F10d is fine elongated lath-like features aligned in one direction, close in character to the deformed F10a and unlike the equiaxed F10b/F10c. The text reads F10d as uniform ultrafine equiaxed grains, so n23 is a real figure-contradicts-text audit.

F11a holds the (0001) pole figure and the IPF map side by side in one panel; the map shows densely packed equiaxed grains of ~1-2 um against its 5 um bar. Splitting the spatial_map reading (o7) from the orientation_distribution reading (o8) on the same panel id is the right handling of a two-kind panel.

Max=3.85 is printed under the F11a pole figure and the density maximum sits off-centre toward TD, as the node says. The panel carries no as-received or as-ECAPed pole figure, which confirms the n24 audit; the packet's OCR cue turning the 4.57 mrd maximum into a '4.57 um scale bar' is a packet defect the staff already flagged.

F13 opened: the 423K-8+373K-3+25us-10min curve yields near 330 MPa, peaks at ~448 MPa and ends at true strain ~0.148, above the other two (peaks ~370 MPa at 0.17 and ~357 MPa at 0.195). Every number in the node is on the panel.

review.audit_summary: Five audit nodes, at the budget, each bounding a different spine claim: n22 (sub-2 um grain claims rest on optical panels that cannot resolve them) and n23 with OBS o5 both qualify the grain-size claim n14, n24 qualifies the texture claim n15, and the n25 contrast branch sets the 89 um starting state against it. n23 is a contradiction and is labelled as one; n22 and n24 are not-resolved findings and are labelled as such. Spine is 20 nodes, at the ceiling, and the extra length is earned: the screening ECAP trials (n7a -> n11 -> n10) motivate the down-select n9 that the rest of the route depends on. The trade-off n18 is closed properly with a counteracts edge from the lost dislocation strengthening n27. No invented panel ids.
